text.name: AutoPlay
text.titlePass: AutoPlay is off for all drives
text.why: AutoPlay opens or runs what is on a USB stick or disc as soon as it is plugged in, before you have looked at it.
fix: Open Settings > Bluetooth & devices > AutoPlay and turn AutoPlay off for yourself.
For the whole PC, tell IT: the policy is "Turn off Autoplay", set to All drives.

absent.found: Not configured for the whole PC (Windows default: AutoPlay on)

text.name: AutoRun commands
text.titlePass: Drives cannot start programs by themselves
text.titleFail: Drives can offer to start programs by themselves
text.why: An autorun command on a USB stick or disc names a program to start. Malware on removable drives relies on it.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Set the default behavior for AutoRun", set to "Do not execute any autorun commands".

absent.found: Not configured (Windows default: the user is asked)

text.name: Elevated installs (PC)
text.titlePass: Installers do not get administrator rights by default
text.titleFail: The PC lets installers run with administrator rights
text.why: With this policy on, any user or any malware can install software with full control of the PC by wrapping it in an installer.
fix: Tell IT: the policy "Always install with elevated privileges" must be disabled.
It is set for the PC in the key shown in the details.

text.name: Elevated installs (user)
text.titlePass: Your installers do not get administrator rights by default
text.titleFail: Your account lets installers run with administrator rights
text.why: Together with the same policy for the PC, any program you run can install software with full control of the PC.
fix: Tell IT: the policy "Always install with elevated privileges" must be disabled.
It is set for your account in the key shown in the details.

text.name: Printer driver installs
text.titlePass: Only administrators can install printer drivers
text.why: A printer driver runs deep inside Windows. Letting any user install one was the opening for the PrintNightmare attacks.
fix: Tell IT: the value RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators shown in the details must be 1 or absent.
If printers stop installing afterwards, IT can pre-install their drivers.

text.name: Print spooler connection encryption
text.titlePass: Connections to the print spooler must be encrypted
text.titleFail: The print spooler accepts unencrypted connections
text.why: The print spooler is a favourite target for attacks over the network. Requiring encrypted, signed-in connections shuts out the weakest of them.
fix: Tell IT: nothing on a current PC needs this switched off.
It is the value RpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled of the Print key shown in the details; it must be 1 or absent.

text.name: Print spooler Redirection Guard
text.titlePass: The print spooler does not follow file redirections
text.titleFail: The print spooler follows file redirections
text.why: The spooler runs with full rights. Redirection Guard stops links from tricking it into writing files where it should not.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Administrative Templates > Printers.
Set "Configure Redirection Guard" to Not configured, or to Enabled with Redirection Guard Enabled.

text.name: Files installed with printers
text.titlePass: Printers can bring only colour profiles with them
text.titleFail: Printers can install any files they bring with them
text.why: A shared printer can make every PC that connects to it copy files. Limiting these to colour profiles keeps it from planting programs.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Administrative Templates > Printers.
Set "Manage processing of Queue-specific files" to Not configured, or limit it to color profiles.

absent.found: Not configured (Windows default: colour profiles only)

text.name: Printer drivers over HTTP
text.titlePass: Printer drivers are never downloaded over plain HTTP
text.titleFail: Printer drivers can be downloaded over plain HTTP
text.why: A driver fetched over plain HTTP can be swapped on the way, and printer drivers run with full rights.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Administrative Templates > System > Internet Communication Management.
Under Internet Communication settings, enable "Turn off downloading of print drivers over HTTP".

text.name: Plug-in devices and memory access
text.titlePass: Plug-in devices without memory protection are blocked
text.titleFail: Plug-in devices without memory protection are allowed
text.why: Thunderbolt and similar devices can read memory directly. This blocks the ones Windows cannot fence off, on PCs that support Kernel DMA Protection.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Administrative Templates > System > Kernel DMA Protection.
Set the enumeration policy to Enabled, with Block all.
Older docks and adapters may stop working: try them afterwards.

absent.found: Not configured (Windows default: allowed after sign-in)
